data.cultural_impact: In Hinduism, the term "Khaja" is primarily used in the context of Lord Khajravan, who is an avatar of Lord Hanuman. This name signifies strength, courage, and protection. Lord Khajravan is believed to be the presiding deity of the forests and is often invoked for safety during travels. He is also known as the Lord of the Nagueshwar Temple in Maharashtra, India.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hinduism, Lord Khajravan represents the divine energy that guides us through our spiritual journey and removes the obstacles that hinder our progress. He is a symbol of unwavering devotion to Lord Rama and offers us the strength to overcome adversity. Lord Khajravan is also revered as the guardian of the dharma (moral laws) and serves as a reminder of our duty to uphold righteousness and truth.

historical_references.reference: The Khajas were a royal Rajput clan of the Chauhan confederacy, who ruled over the area that is now Rajasthan from the 11th to the 13th centuries. They were known for their military prowess and were significant contributors to medieval Indian culture.

historical_references.reference: Khajurao, a town in Madhya Pradesh, India, is famous for its group of temples called the Khajurao temples. These temples, built between 950 and 1050 AD during the Chandela Dynasty, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and are renowned for their intricate carvings and sensual and erotic themes.
